title: Strong intervalley mixing between copropagating quantum Hall edge channels in a silicon MOSFET
abstract: Copropagating quantum Hall edge channels provide a promising platform for compact electron interferometry and flying quantum states. In silicon, the valley degree of freedom offers a natural alternative to spin-resolved edge channels because spin-flip scattering is strongly suppressed by the weak spin-orbit interaction. Here, we investigate interchannel transitions between copropagating valley edge channels in a double-layer-gated silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor. With the bulk filling factor set to $ν=2$, two spin-polarized valley edge channels are brought into close proximity near a depleted side gate. We observe strong intervalley mixing, with a transition probability close to 1/2, indicating nearly complete equilibration between the two valley edge channels. In contrast, interchannel transport between edge channels with different spin orientations shows negligible transition probability, consistent with suppressed spin-flip scattering in silicon. These results demonstrate that intervalley coupling at a Si/SiO$_2$ interface can provide a beam-splitter-like operation for copropagating valley edge channels, establishing a key building block toward compact silicon quantum Hall interferometers.
summary: The researchers demonstrated strong intervalley mixing between edge channels in a silicon MOSFET operating in the Quantum Hall regime. This finding establishes that the valley degree of freedom acts as an effective 'valley beam splitter' for quantum information processing. The results confirm this capability while simultaneously showing that spin-flip processes are strongly suppressed, making Si a promising platform.
main_problem: The study investigates strong intervalley mixing between copropagating quantum Hall edge channels to establish a fundamental building block for compact silicon quantum Hall interferometers.
main_result: Strong intervalley mixing was observed with a transition probability near 1/2, while interchannel transport requiring spin-flip scattering showed negligible probability, confirming the utility of valley degrees of freedom in Si MOSFETs.
method: Measurements were performed on a double-layer-gated Si MOSFET in the Quantum Hall regime using low-frequency lock-in techniques to measure conductance and extract transition probabilities via Landauer–Büttiker formalism.
model_or_system: The physical system is a double-layer-gated Silicon Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (Si MOSFET) operating under high magnetic fields in the Quantum Hall regime. The valley degree of freedom is exploited as an alternative to spin for channel manipulation.
key_observables: Transition probability ($T_v$) between valley edge channels, and transition probability ($T_s$) for spin-flip interchannel transport.
